Reaching 1,000 active members from your current base of 600 by next October is mathematically challenging under current metrics, but entirely realistic if you fix retention alongside acquisition. Right now, your 18% monthly churn erodes growth rapidly. You lose roughly 100 members a month, meaning your 90 new sign-ups result in a net monthly loss. 

To hit your goal, choose two specific initiatives: launch an annual plan and double the Instagram ad budget. 

The annual plan stabilizes cash flow, lowers initial friction through a discounted upfront commitment, and directly counters early churn by locking members in for twelve months. Pairing this with a doubled ad budget scales your top-of-funnel acquisition, leveraging your proven 110-dollar acquisition cost to push monthly sign-ups from 90 to roughly 180. Avoid cutting the price to 49 dollars, which damages perceived value and requires massive volume increases to maintain revenue. Reject adding more live classes and meal tools, as they inflate operational overhead without addressing the core driver of early cancellation: onboarding friction.

Your concrete next steps are to design a compelling annual pricing tier offering two months free, and immediately upgrade your ad creatives to handle the increased spend efficiently. 

Material assumptions rely on your ad conversion efficiency remaining stable as spend doubles, and that onboarding sequences are tightened to keep early churn from spiking as volume increases. 

Decision criteria to re-evaluate this strategy include monitoring whether the annual plan adoption hits at least 15 percent of total sales within ninety days, and tracking if your acquisition cost climbs above 140 dollars, which would necessitate pausing ad scaling until creative fatigue is resolved.
